business: SEGMENT: PI car accident intake, Pleasanton (Shotland pilot)
prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear about your accident — that’s stressful. I can’t pick one specific lawyer for you, but I can tell you how to find the best attorney for your situation, what to ask, what to do right now, and offer to help shortlist local options if you want.

Quick immediate steps
- Get medical care now and follow doctors’ orders. Your health and medical records are the most important evidence.
- Call the police and get a copy of the police report or at least the report number.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries, traffic signs, dashcam/phone video, witness names/contacts.
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other driver’s insurer until you’ve talked to a lawyer if your injuries are significant.
- Keep all bills, receipts, pay stubs (for lost wages), and a daily journal of symptoms and recovery.

Important California deadlines (act quickly)
- Personal injury: generally 2 years from the accident to file suit (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. §335.1).
- Property damage: often 3 years.
- Wrongful death: 2 years.
- Claims against a government entity: often 6 months to file a written claim first (these deadlines are very strict).
Missing a deadline can bar your case, so consult an attorney soon.

How to choose the right lawyer
Look for a lawyer who:
- Focuses on car-accident/personal-injury cases (not a generalist).
- Has experience in Alameda County and with California law and insurance practices.
- Handles cases similar to yours (minor injury vs. catastrophic/brain/spine/wrongful death).
- Has trial experience—many cases settle, but you want someone who will take the case to trial if needed.
- Works on contingency (common: usually 33%–40% of recovery, plus costs; get the exact percent and conditions in writing).
- Communicates clearly and promptly and names who will be handling daily work (attorney vs. paralegal).
- Has verifiable client reviews, published results, and good standing with the State Bar.

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific settlement or immediate large payout.
- High-pressure tactics to sign a contract immediately.
- Poor communication or evasive answers about fees/trial experience.
- Asking you to sign medical releases that are overly broad without explaining them.

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How many years have you handled car-accident personal injury cases?
- What percentage of your practice is car-accidents/personal injury?
- Have you handled cases like mine? What results have you achieved?
- Will you take cases to trial? How many trials have you done?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your fee (contingency %)? What costs will I be responsible for if we don’t recover?
- How do you communicate (phone/email/text) and how often will I get updates?
- Do you advance medical, expert, and litigation costs?
- Can you provide references from recent clients?

What a good attorney will do for you
- Investigate the accident, preserve evidence and witness statements.
- Coordinate medical treatment and, where needed, medical liens.
- Handle insurance communications and negotiations.
- Evaluate full damages (medical, future care, lost wages, pain & suffering).
- Advise whether to accept settlement or file suit.

Where to find attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association referral service.
- State Bar of California “Find a Lawyer” (to confirm license/discipline).
- Local reviews on Google/Yelp, Martindale-Hubbell, or AVVO for reputation and peer ratings.
- Ask local friends, family, or medical providers for referrals.

If you’d like, I can:
- Help you shortlist 3–5 local Pleasanton/Alameda County lawyers based on experience and reviews (I’ll need details about your case and preferences).
- Draft a short script/email you can use to contact lawyers and what documents to bring to consultations.
- Review fee agreements or answer any specific questions you get from an attorney.

If you want me to shortlist attorneys, tell me: date of accident, nature/severity of injuries, whether the police report exists, whether there are insurance disputes, and whether the other party was a government vehicle.
